statement: Let (u, v) be a dual pair and 0 < t < 1. Then Qtu = −Q1−tv ∈ C1,1(M), with almost-everywhere bounds − Cg 1 − t g ≤ Hess Qtu ≤ Cg t g. If (xt(z), pt(z)) = F−1 t (z) and Φs is geodesic flow on TM, then (xt(z), pt(z)) = Φ−t(z, grad Qtu(z)). In particular, the pole and momentum maps are Lipschitz with constants depending only on M, g, t. There are also rt, bt > 0, depending only on M, g, t, such that every z = expx(tp), p ∈ ∂u(x), satisfies u(x′ ) + ct(x′ , z) ≥ u(x) + ct(x, z) + btd(x, x′ )2 if d(x, x′ ) < rt. All these constants are uniform when t ranges in a compact subinterval of (0, 1).
